newsitem.title: USA: Warm weather, below normal rainfall in Florida.
newsitem.headline: Warm weather, below normal rainfall in Florida.

text.p: Above average temperatures and very little rain hit the Florida citrus belt last week, but cool nightime temperatures prevented citrus trees from producing new growth, the Florida Agricultural Statistics Service (FASS), said.

Temperatures for the week ended Dec 29 fell to the low 30s in some Panhandle, northern Peninsula and central Peninsula areas. The average low temperatures for the week remained in the 40s to 50s (degrees Fahrenheit), however.
The highest temperatures soared in the 70s and 80s, FASS said.
Meantime, caretakers continue to cut cover crops prior to harvest, and some rust mite sprays are being applied to crops going to the fresh trade.
FASS reported an estimated 141,000 boxes of navel oranges were harvested in the week ended December 28, down from 508,000 boxes the previous week and 699,000 boxes in the week ended December 15.
An estimated 5,840,000 boxes of early and mid oranges were harvested in the week ended December 28, down from 9,614,000 boxes the prior week and 9,489,000 boxes the week ended December 15, FASS said.
